scope: Static preview/initial or explicit disk-frame object composition; no triggers, collision/steel, ticks, gameplay scheduling, audio, platform screen or actual DOS execution certification.
pixel_encoding: One byte per row-major pixel: low 4 bits global palette index; bit 4 original terrain provenance; bit 5 object provenance. Transparent=0. Object and terrain flags survive overlap. These are drawing flags, not physics.
palette_policy: Object/game RGB8: fixed DOS palette raw6<<2, upper bank current terrain raw6*255//63; index 7 copies index 8, special index 8 is (124,124,0). Terrain RGB8: normal raw6*255//63, VGASPEC raw6<<2. An object pixel selects the object palette; uncovered terrain selects its local terrain palette. Separate banks preserve Lemmix special-level RGB differences.
rgba_encoding: RGBA8, alpha 255 for terrain or object, transparent all zero; use object palette if object bit set, otherwise terrain palette with local index=global-8.
reference_policy: Lemmix static RenderWorld: only-on-terrain pass then other objects, stable file order in each; only-on-terrain before no-overwrite, original terrain bit vs any occupied destination, vertical flip before clipping. Explicit source mask preserves opaque black; original 540 frames have no mask-vs-nonzero difference.
frame_policy: Preview reads exact absolute preview window; Initial uses GROUND first_frame, not a certified gameplay-start state; Explicit indexes original 32 slots without wrapping. All 54 original slots have preview==first_frame. Unaligned synthetic preview windows are supported directly, unlike Lemmix integer division.
verification: Independent Python freshly unpacks all 94 relevant original DAT sections, reconstructs terrain/objects and compares 80 base geometries x 2 frame choices / 240 catalog scenes / 60825600 indexed/provenance pixels, RGB hashes, palettes and routes. Real pinned TS GroundReader/LevelReader/MapObject/Animation/ObjectManager/GroundRenderer/Frame confirm normalized occupied RGBA; draw policy and palette differences are recorded separately.
